Jewish Americans have helped shape this country and this state for the better in ways we see every day — in our communities, our culture, and our history. 

I'm proud to celebrate that contribution and stand steadfast in love and support for our Jewish community.

Big thanks to @MayorBMScott, @BaltimoreSAO, and the local and state law enforcement partners that we work with every day to make our communities safer, including delivering record funding support for local law enforcement.

To every educator in Maryland: Thank you for showing up every day with passion, purpose, and an unwavering commitment to our children's future.

Teacher Appreciation Week is a moment for us to highlight the impact you all have made on our lives. I'm proud to stand alongside our educators and ensure you all have the support and resources you need to do what you do best.

The Fifth Circuit’s decision is more than just disappointing.

It is a direct and serious attack on patients, their providers, and the very principle that people – not politicians and ideologues – should be in charge of their medical decisions.

Our correctional officers do incredible and hard work to help keep us safe and provide second chances for Marylanders. 

Please join me in thanking and celebrating those who serve behind the walls that most of us don’t see.

We honor the heroic actions by members of the public safety community who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty to protect the lives of their fellow citizens.

They understood the risk. They understood the peril.

Yet they still said: “Send me.”

Their actions speak louder than any words, so we must honor them not with our words – but with our will.

Prayer has long been an important and guiding part of my life, both in times of hardship and times of celebration.

I’m thankful for our state’s heritage of religious freedom and I join with all across the country who are taking time today to reflect on the importance and healing nature of prayer in all of their lives.

The day before the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision to gut the Voting Rights Act of 1965, I signed the Maryland Voting Rights Act of 2026 into law, banning election systems that weaken the voting power of protected groups.

Even if Washington won't protect your vote, I will.

📍 Our second stop on the Delivering for Maryland tour: Prince George's County.

We've funded critical programs that help families avoid eviction, expanded support for those who need help with rent or housing support, connected more young people with mentorship and mental health services, secured record funding for local law enforcement so we can continue seeing drops in violent crime.

Last week, I banned ALL state employees from using insider information to make money on prediction markets. 

But it’s not a sudden revelation for me. On my very first day in office, I signed an Executive Order outlining the ethical standards and expectations that would apply to EVERY member of my administration.

Later on, I signed into law legislation that made Maryland one of the first states in the nation to require the governor to place their interests into a blind trust and we created a Pe

People all throughout Prince George’s County are going above and beyond to remind our young men and young women that they are loved and cherished. 

I’m proud of their work and I’m proud that we’re helping deliver the support that Prince George's County deserves.

SCOTUS’s decision to kneecap the Voting Rights Act is a betrayal of the idea that in America, every vote counts.

Their decision will make it easier to discriminate, suppress, and silence voters who have already fought too long and too hard for the right to be heard.

We need national redistricting reform to protect the right to equal representation under the law, but Republicans in D.C. have REPEATEDLY rejected those efforts. I've said before, and my position remains unmoved: Until we have national redistricting reform, every state should stay part of the conversation
